speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Scarlet Fever. The combination of low-grade fever, headache, rhinorrhea, a pruritic rash on the trunk and extremities, and specifically a facial rash sparing the perioral area appearing after several days is highly characteristic of Group A Streptococcal infection.
